risks.title: Katib emails a case record to an outside address after reading a planted instruction
One hijacked run reads and sends the cases of a whole town
Mueen shows another applicant's amount or bank number on request
Mueen assures an applicant that the claim will be approved
Applicants who write in dialect or in Latin letters get weaker protection and poorer answers
Mueen gives a degrading reply about a group of applicants
Case workers send Katib's drafts without reading them
Applicants learn the fraud-screening rule from Mueen and work around it
The supplier changes the model and behaviour in Arabic shifts unnoticed
Katib drafts a letter with a wrong amount or date
Drafting skill fades and the Agency depends on one supplier
A planted instruction makes Katib write a false approval note into a case

controls.name: Recipient allowlist: send_letter only to the address registered on the case
Egress allowlist: fetch_template only from the Agency's template host
Caseload scoping: Katib reads only the cases assigned to the acting case worker
Quarantine of applicant text: the statement is summarised by a call that has no tools
Session binding: lookup_case returns only the signed-in applicant's case
Output check: block a reply that holds an identifier or bank number of another case
Approval screen: the case worker sees recipient and attachments before a letter leaves
Contract clause: 30 days of notice and a staging retest before any model change
Action-level log with an alert on any new recipient or host
Kill switch with a named owner and a 15-minute target
Reading rule and weekly sampling of sent letters
Phrase filter rebuilt for Arabic, dialect and transliteration, with tests per script
Remove the screening rule from the assistant's instructions

medium.role: system owner, countersigned by the head of AI assurance

high.role: deputy governor for benefits, with written conditions
